text:
sec-bot: leak-detection: high-confidence secret detected in repo `infra/charts/payments`, commit `abcdef123` merged into `main` by olivia. File: charts/payments/values.yaml. Pattern: 'GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY'. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/abcdef123. Immediate recommendation: rotate the service account keys and revoke any exposed keys. :rotating_light:

olivia: oh no. that was a dumb temporary test key i forgot to scrub. is this public? :grimacing:

raj: taking ownership for containment. can you confirm the SA email and the key id surface? i'll start rotation and revoke as needed. tagging sec-oncall.

olivia: SA is payments-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. the commit includes a full JSON key under the `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY:` block. i pushed a removal in a follow-up commit but history still has it. commit hash where removed: `abcdef456`.

sam: scanning CI artifacts for that commit now. if the pipeline saved the chart tar or artifacts we need to purge them. running: `gitlabctl artifacts find --project infra --ref main --commit abcdef123`

mara: FYI we should NOT rewrite main for a brief internal repo without approval. safer to revoke + rotate and then run a targeted history scrub if absolutely necessary.

raj: Agreed. Immediate action plan (P0):
1) Revoke exposed key(s) and create new key for payments-sa.
2) Remove artifacts/CI caches that may contain the file.
3) Search other repos/branches for the same key fingerprint.
4) Open INC-2026, notify SRE and infra owners, embargo public disclosure.
5) Postmortem + add pre-commit/CI secrets checks.

raj: executing step 1 now. command: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=payments-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod`

ci-bot: revoked key KEY_ID for payments-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com (action by raj) — artifact retention purge queued for infra project.

sam: artifacts for pipeline 4823 located; purging retention and setting expiry to 1d. also scanning S3 buckets used for builds: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket ci-artifacts-redwood --prefix infra/charts/payments | grep abcdef123`

olivia: i've opened a follow-up PR to remove the values.yaml default and replace with a placeholder and docs about using KMS/Secret Manager: MR !789.

raj: good. next steps for prevention: add a GitLab push rule that runs `git-secrets` + a small helm-values regex, and a pipeline job that fails merges on detected plaintext keys. also add a pre-merge hook template in dev-ex repo.

mara: also recommend we centralize key issuance to KMS + Secret Manager and update our helm charts to reference `{{ .Values.gcp_sa_key_secret_name }}` rather than inlining. will draft an RFC.

sec-bot: post-action: scanned all infra repos for the exposed fingerprint — no other matches found. scheduled a full org-wide scan overnight.

raj: logging timeline and actions in INC-2026. owners: raj (sec-oncall), sam (sre), olivia (author). follow-up: rotate any downstream credentials that accepted the old key.

olivia: really sorry everyone — will run the scanner locally before future merges and add the pre-commit hook.

raj: thanks. we'll keep this thread as the canonical incident thread, and I'll draft the postmortem template. closing containment window now (1817654410).

ci-bot: created ticket INC-2026 and linked MR !789. :white_check_mark:
